newsitem.title: UK: Commodity regulators to meet Nov 25/26 in London.
newsitem.headline: Commodity regulators to meet Nov 25/26 in London.

text.p: Financial regulators of the main commodity markets are to hold a meeting in London on November 25-26, an official at Britain's leading market watchdog the Securities and Investment Board (SIB) confirmed.
The SIB official said that the meeting will focus on futures exchanges with a deliverable commodity contract.
In May last year a similar regulators' meeting was held in Windsor, England after the crash of Barings Bank.
Regulators then agreed on exchanging information, mainly focusing on financial futures.

But brokers said additional information sharing is needed for physically deliverable commodities as off-market trading either in the Over-the-Counter (OTC) market or in physical commodities can play a vital part in determining prices.

The meeting, triggered by the huge $2.6 billion losses in copper trading made by Japan's Sumitomo Corp, is expected to be the first in an ongoing series aimed at improving co-operation between regulators especially in times of crisis.

The SIB, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) and Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI), are co-hosting the meeting which was outlined on September 5 at the annual commodity conference in Buergenstock, Switzerland.
The meeting will be between regulators and will not include exchanges, the official noted.
Regulators from other countries with significant international commodity exchanges will also be invited, the SIB official said.
